<STATEMENT>
For any two formulas φ and ψ, the meaning of φ ⋎ ψ is equal to the disjunction of the meanings of φ and ψ.

</STATEMENT>
<PROOF>
The equivalence is immediate by definition, as the meaning of the disjunction of two formulas is defined to be the disjunction of their individual meanings. This follows directly from the way the connective is implemented and the properties it satisfies.

<STATEMENT>

For any two formulas \( \varphi \) and \( \psi \), the interpretation of their meet (which corresponds to the logical "and") in a structure \( \mathcal{M} \) is equal to the meet of their individual interpretations in \( \mathcal{M} \). In other words, \( (\varphi \, \text{and} \, \psi)^{\mathcal{M}} = (\varphi^{\mathcal{M}} \, \text{and} \, \psi^{\mathcal{M}}) \).

</STATEMENT>
<PROOF>

This equality holds by definition of how the interpretation of formulas is extended to logical connectives. Specifically, the meet operation corresponds to the logical "and" connective, and the interpretation of this connective is defined to be the same as the Boolean meet operation on the truth values in the structure \( \mathcal{M} \). Therefore, the equation is satisfied by the very definition of the interpretation function, and no further proof is required beyond recognizing this fact.
